sources.entry: Kan - Flexible kanban app that helps you organise work, track progress, and deliver results (alternative to Trello). (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Kan is an open-source, self-hostable kanban project management app positioned as an alternative to Trello.
summary.what_it_does: Kan is a Trello-style kanban board app built with Next.js, tRPC, and Drizzle ORM on PostgreSQL. Its listed features include board visibility controls, workspace member invitations, importing Trello boards, labels and filters, card comments, an activity log of card changes, and reusable board templates. Self-hosting is covered via Docker Compose, which runs a migration service, the web app, and a Postgres 15 database. Optional settings cover email via SMTP, Redis-based rate limiting, OAuth and generic OIDC login, and S3-compatible storage for uploads. The README also describes an MCP server (run via npx) that lets AI clients control a Kan instance.
use_cases: self-hosted kanban board for a team
replacing Trello with an open-source tool
tracking project tasks and card progress
managing team projects with comments and activity history
how_to_run: Create a .env file with the required environment variables (see Environment Variables section)
Create or use the provided docker-compose.yml with the migrate, web, and postgres services
Alternatively for development: git clone the repo, then pnpm install
Copy .env.example to .env, then run pnpm db:migrate
Start the dev server with pnpm dev
notable: Official Railway one-click deployment template in addition to Docker Compose
Includes an MCP server so AI clients can read and control a Kan instance
Supports multiple login methods including Google, GitHub, Discord, and generic OIDC
Pre-built Docker images published on GHCR
caveats: Some features, such as integrations, are listed as coming soon
Trello import requires Trello app API key and secret to be configured
Self-hosting requires setting up PostgreSQL and environment variables; Redis and S3 are optional extras
keywords: share a task board with my team
